question.leadin: Answer the following about advancements in space exploration.
question.text: The first American human spaceflight program shared its name with this planet, the closest planet to the Sun.
question.clue: The number 7 featured in the names of every vehicle used, including Friendship 7, flown by John Glenn, and Freedom 7, flown by Alan Shepard, the first American in space.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
swap.text: This president claimed that his wife, Pat, "doesn't have a mink coat" in his "Checkers" speech. This man was later forced to resign over the Watergate scandal, despite declaring "I am not a crook".
swap.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

question.text: This commander of the Apollo 11 mission, the first man to set foot on the moon, passed away in August 2012.
question.clue: JFK's wish for a man on the moon was fulfilled when this astronaut made "one giant leap for mankind," becoming the first American on the moon.

swap.leadin: B-26 bombers were repainted to look like FAR planes to maintain the illusion that this event was operated only by rebel troops.
swap.text: Name this failed 1961 invasion that attempted to overthrow the Communist dictator of Cuba.
swap.answerHtml: Bay of Pigs invasion (accept Operation Zapata; accept word forms for invasion)
swap.clue: This event's failure led Allen Dulles to be forced to resign.

question.leadin: Fawn Hall attempted to destroy evidence for this scandal.
question.text: Name this scandal in which funds from the sale of weapons to the Middle East were diverted to Nicaraguan rebels.
question.clue: The main perpetrator of this event was exposed when his letters to John Poindexter were discovered.

swap.text: One month after the Daisy Ad aired, a future California governor gave this speech in favor of Goldwater on the TV show Rendezvous with Destiny. This speech claims that the US must go "up to man's age-old dream" or "down to the ant heap of totalitarianism."
swap.clue: It was known as "The Speech" while being perfected over a series of deliveries to city Chambers of Commerce, before it was finally delivered on television by the host of GE Theater.

question.text: One notable Minnesotan politician was this Carter vice president and opponent of Ronald Reagan in the 1984 presidential election.
question.clue: In 1984, Ronald Reagan won re-election over this Democrat-Jimmy Carter's former vice-president-by winning every state except this man's home state, Minnesota.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the ultra-right wing, anti-communist John Birch Society.
swap.text: The Society split over supporting this Republican candidate in 1964. This man's slogan "In your heart, you know he's right" was mocked with "In your guts, you know he's nuts" by LBJ's campaign, which also ran the Daisy Ad against him.
swap.clue: Ronald Reagan gave his "A Time for Choosing" speech in support of this politician.

question.leadin: This event was sparked by thousands of people who rushed the Peruvian embassy trying to seek asylum.
question.text: Name this 1980 event in which large numbers of people, many of them released prisoners, boarded ramshackle crafts headed to Florida from the namesake town.
question.answerHtml: Mariel Boatlift [prompt on but DO NOT REVEAL Cuban Boatlift]
question.clue: Some participants in this event staged a riot at Fort Chaffee, Arkansas, which briefly derailed the career of Governor Bill Clinton.

swap.leadin: The economist Nathaniel Baum-Snow found that this program led to a 17% reduction in the population of major American cities between 1950 and 1990.
swap.text: Name this massive federal project built partly for defense purposes. The Overtown neighborhood of Miami lost much of its population due to this project.
swap.answerHtml: Interstate Highway System [prompt on highway; accept but DO NOT REVEAL Dwight D. Eisenhower National System of Interstate and Defense Highways]
swap.clue: Construction for this project, originally designed for quick military deployment, began in 1956.

question.text: Earlier, the Unemployed Council, a subsidiary of this political party, conducted the Ford Hunger Strike. The Hollywood Ten were blacklisted for having affiliations with this party.
question.clue: Freedom of speech was incorporated in a case against a founder of this organization named Benjamin Gitlow, who later testified against this organization in front of HUAC ("HYOO-ack").

swap.text: In the 1992 campaign, this Texas billionaire ran as an independent and garnered 19% of the popular vote.
swap.clue: This man promised there would be a "giant sucking sound" as jobs went to Mexico when speaking out against NAFTA.

question.leadin: Identify some things related to nattering nabobs of negativity.
question.text: That phrase was uttered by this Vice President under Nixon, who was forced to resign due to allegations of extortion and bribery dating to his time as Governor of Maryland.
question.clue: His conservatism was further seen in a later position, in which he mocked liberals as "nattering nabobs."

swap.text: This promoter of the NRA and mentor of Hugh Johnson was a Wall Street financier who served on the War Industries Board during World War I. He proposed a namesake nuclear weapons-regulation plan after World War II.
swap.clue: He supports public funding for college students and identifies as a democratic socialist.

question.leadin: Following a 1970s civil war, many people of this ethnicity settled in the communities of Eau Claire and Wausau, Wisconsin.
question.text: Name this ethnicity of nearly 400,000 Americans, many of whom came to the US after a "Secret War." In the 1980s, people of this ethnicity relocated from refugee camps to Merced.
question.answerHtml: Hmong Americans [or Hmoob Mes Kas; prompt on Miao, though this term is considered a pejorative)

swap.text: This senior Senator from Tennessee was Adlai Stevenson's running mate in 1956, and he led an eponymous senate committee that investigated organized crime.
swap.clue: He also sponsored a bill that tightened up the Clayton Antitrust Act and ended vertical mergers, along with Emmanuel Celler.

question.leadin: Its formation was presaged by Truman's decision to desegregate the armed forces and it was made official in 1948 after the passage of a civil rights platform.
question.text: Identify this third party that met in Birmingham, Alabama, to nominate Strom Thurmond for President.
question.answer: Dixiecrats or States' Rights Democratic Party
question.clue: Members had earlier walked out of another party's convention after a speech by Hubert Humphrey.

swap.text: The investigation into Agnew's corruption was headed by this Attorney General under Nixon, who chose to resign rather than fire the special prosecutor Archibald Cox during the Saturday Night Massacre.
swap.clue: This Attorney General refused to fire Cox and resigned from the administration, though he later urged Bork to carry out the order.

question.leadin: Hugh Johnson helped prepare the original one. FTPE.
question.text: Speaker of the House Champ Clark was a staunch opponent of this act, which initiated the first military draft. Variations of this act were passed in 1940, 1948, and 1967.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 1988 Democratic National Convention.
swap.text: This speaker introduced the anti-George H.W. Bush zinger "Where was George?" His own presidential aspirations were probably terminated by the 1969 Chappaquiddick incident.
swap.clue: After a tribute to him at the 2008 DNC, he gave a speech saying that "the dream lives on," and in 2009, he left the Senate Judiciary Committee.
